passage:
Saturday. At the community centre final, Aditi quietly moved her counter two squares ahead while Ishita turned to sip water. She won, and everyone clapped. Ishita hugged her.

Sunday. The trophy sat on her shelf like a stone. She couldn't finish breakfast, and every time her mother said, "So proud," her stomach dropped.

Wednesday. Aditi went to Coach Meena's office, hands cold. "I cheated in the final," she said. "I moved my counter." The coach was quiet, then said the trophy would go to Ishita and Aditi would sit out the next tournament. Aditi cried, but on the walk home her chest felt lighter, like a fresh start.

qa.q: What did Aditi move during the final?
What did the trophy feel like to Aditi on Sunday, and why?
qa.a: Heavy, like a stone, because guilt was working on her: she couldn't finish breakfast and her stomach dropped when her mother said "So proud."

qa.q: Why was going to the coach better than hiding it?
qa.a: Hiding it would let the guilt grow, while admitting it meant accepting a consequence and starting clean.

qa.q: How might Ishita feel when she learns about the trophy?
qa.a: Possibly hurt by the cheating but glad to hear the truth, since she had hugged Aditi believing the win was fair.

grounding: A child cheats and wins, feels the trophy is heavy, admits it to the coach, accepts a consequence and starts clean.

passage:
At the Hyderabad inter-school chess tournament, Rafiq touched his knight, then quietly moved his rook instead while Minakshi looked away. It won him the game and the trophy.
Everyone clapped. Minakshi shook his hand. "Well played."
At home, the trophy sat on his shelf. Rafiq couldn't look at it. It felt heavy, like a stone in his stomach.
On Monday he went to the chess coach. "Sir, I broke the touch-move rule in the final. Minakshi should have won."
The coach was quiet. Then he said, "Thank you for telling me. You'll have to return the trophy, and apologise to Minakshi."
Rafiq nodded. For the first time in days, he could breathe.

qa.q: How did Rafiq feel about the trophy at home?
qa.a: He felt guilty and heavy, unable to look at it, like a stone in his stomach.

qa.q: What did Rafiq do to start clean?
qa.a: He admitted it to the coach, accepted returning the trophy and agreed to apologise to Minakshi.

qa.q: How might Minakshi feel when she hears the truth?
qa.a: Minakshi may feel surprised and a little hurt, but she might also respect Rafiq for owning up.

grounding: A boy cheats to win a trophy and feels its weight; he admits it to the coach, accepts the consequence and starts clean.

passage:
"Coach Alka, can I talk to you?"
"Of course, Nilesh. What's up?"
"The race last week. The 400 metres."
"You won. Well done."
"I didn't really. I cut the corner on the back straight. Nobody saw."
Coach Alka put down her clipboard. "I see."
"The medal's been in my drawer. I can't even look at it."
"That's your conscience telling you something."
"I know. What happens now?"
"You'll give the medal to Harish, who came second. And you'll sit out the next meet. But you told me yourself, and that matters."
Nilesh let out a long breath. "Okay. Thank you."

qa.q: What did Nilesh cut on the back straight?
How did Nilesh feel about the medal?
qa.a: He felt guilty, unable to look at it, and kept it hidden in a drawer.

qa.q: What consequence did Coach Alka give?
qa.a: Nilesh would give the medal to Harish and sit out the next meet.

qa.q: How might Coach Alka see Nilesh's confession?
qa.a: Coach Alka values that he told her himself, saying it matters.

grounding: A boy cheats to win a race and the medal feels heavy; he admits it to his coach, accepts a consequence and starts clean.
